name: Focusing Effect
description: When judging a complex outcome, people overweight the salient feature currently in view and neglect the rest of what will matter in real life. What is easy to think about temporarily feels more important than it really is.
design_relevance_note: Shows up in concept testing, feature prioritization, pricing research, relocation/travel/service comparisons, and product decisions where one vivid attribute dominates the judgment of the whole experience.
myth_risk_note: The core focusing-illusion mechanism is real and well-demonstrated by Kahneman and colleagues, but its scope in everyday practitioner usage is often broader than what the peer-reviewed literature specifically validates -- the popular label risks overextending a narrower, well-evidenced effect.
prevalence_note: Common in behavioral-economics and affective-forecasting discussions, and occasionally invoked in product strategy, but much less named in routine UX critique than loss aversion, social proof, or cognitive load.

findings.description: Midwestern and Southern California students reported similar overall life satisfaction, yet participants expected Californians to be happier because salient differences like climate and cultural opportunities were overweighted when judging life in another location — the paper's own 'focusing illusion' conclusion.
findings.source_title: Does Living in California Make People Happy? A Focusing Illusion in Judgments of Life Satisfaction
